result.title: Continuous Ontology Assurance through External Resources -- An Ontology Engineering Method with a Case Study in Software Language Engineering
result.summary: Domain ontologies require review against knowledge recorded in evolving external resources. We propose COATER, a method that manages executable review components called arrows. Each arrow compares a scoped part of an ontology with a relevant resource and reports support or challenges to its axioms. Challenges may prompt proposals for completion, correction, or restructuring and become tasks for human or agent-assisted triage. Per-axiom coverage summarizes the assessments. We illustrate COATER with the FSL ontology in software language engineering (SLE): arrows review language coverage, language conceptualization, and software-engineering activities. An LLM-assisted linkage exercise increases compliance with a defined Wikipedia-linkage policy from 405 to 600 of 600 entities. A structured catalogue of SLE resources organizes review opportunities.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 COATER 方法，用可执行的审查组件「arrows」把领域本体中受范围限定的部分与相关外部资源对照，报告对公理的支持或挑战，并汇总逐公理覆盖度；并以软件语言工程中的 FSL 本体为案例，用 LLM 辅助链接流程提升实体链接合规率。
AI.relevance_reason: 把内部表示（本体公理）与外部资源对照以获取证据、并按单元汇总覆盖度，可能为 latent 推理状态如何与视觉证据核验、以及贡献分配与审查粒度问题提供概念类比，但领域相距较远，线索属推测、需人工核查。
